segments.text: (bright music)
- Hello, everyone, I am Zach Peterson,

coming to you live from
the show floor at PCB West,
and I am joined today by Tristan Ren,

director of operations
at TapRen Solutions.

So TapRen Solutions, you
guys are a newer company

and you are also new to
being on camera with me,
of course, on the channel.
So was like to ask new folks
how did you get into electronics
and how did you start your company?
- Yeah, Zach, thank you for having us.

It's very nice to talk
to you in your interview.
So, we are a very young company.
We started just three, four years ago.
Me and my business partner, Tejas,
we formed a company called TapRen.
We are engineers who met at Intel
and we have a business at heart
and we always looking for solutions
to solve the world's problem.

And at this time, there's
a customer come to us
for supply chain-related issue.
They want to find low cost
and good quality suppliers from the source
to supply their PCB products.
So that's how we started business.

We basically reverse
engineer the whole process,
figure out the whole supply chain, design,
manufacturing, and then we manage
to deliver a good product to the customer.
And then we start, ever since then,

we just like start growing
the business from that point.

So I've been doing
business for three years
and our main focus is on the PCB design
and then electronic supply chain service.
So we manage to deliver high quality,
zero defect and products

with very fast delivery
time to our customer.

- So, when you say you're
managing the supply chain

for your clients, this is
really taking those designs,
taking them and putting them in place
and 'em in the right factory
that's gonna give them the right quality,

the right capabilities, materials,
everything down the list?

- Yes.
- Yeah.

- Yes.
- So, where are you guys
producing it?

- Producing in terms of?
- Yeah, like,
where are you producing PCBs?
- So we have our team based out of Asia
and they handle the purchase

and also enrolling the quality
manufacturer into our system.

So most of our manufacturer
are based out of China,
Malaysia, and India.

So that's where the
manufacturing happens, yeah.

- So what are some of the
biggest misconceptions
that clients have about working
with a company in Asia?

What are some of the
challenges that they face
that causes them to come to you?
- That's a good question.
Yeah, because our customer did ask us

a lot of questions like,
because it's not domestic,

we can't really see, it
sounds like intangible.
Like, how can we make sure everything
is up to the standards we have here.

But me personally, I
travel to China, to Asia

from time to time and meet
with the manufacturer.

I have the local person, who
also our supply chain analyst,
to value the manufacturer.
They have all the certificates, right?

They meet all the aspects,
they're legit companies
and they have legit products
and they also have experience working
with overseas customers.

So that's how our first run
of vetting the business.
And then we always do prototyping,

making sure we handle
the quality lead time,
pricing everything correctly

before we start ramping up
the volume for the customer.
So we go through those process
and adding the extra insurance

and we have, even though
customer's not there seeing

the manufacturer, we send
detailed camera footage,
videos and pictures,
making sure they have a visual inspection.
So, and now, we have a US representative
to update a customer

to make sure they stay
tuned with the production.
- Absolutely. Absolutely.
Yeah, I know going overseas to China
or India can create some challenges.
I mean there's the time zone difference,
which makes it difficult to communicate.

There's the language and
cultural differences.
So I think you being Chinese

or going to China essentially
makes all of that a lot easier

for customers who might
want to produce overseas.
- Exactly, exactly. Definitely.
I'm trying to, right now,

I'm the main person
- Yeah.
- handling the insurance,

but our team is growing, so
we're gonna have more people
who can, like for a specific project,
we'll have our signed person to handle
that customer account too.

- Absolutely.
- Yeah.

- So of course, we've
talked about it many times

on the channel and of
course it's in the news,
which is tariffs and export control
and these kinds of things.
And then the shifting global supply chain.

Have customers been coming
to you because of tariffs?

Have you seen that drop off?
Have you seen that ramp up?
How has some of the issues
with tariffs changed your business
and how has it changed your approach?
- Yeah, that is a very legit concern.
And I think for the majority of the year,

ever since the new
announcement with the tariff,
there's definitely created a lot
of uncertainties in the business.

Even though a lot of
customer, they are not dealing
with the import-export on a daily basis,
there's a fear everywhere in the industry

because they know it's
gonna float up the cost.
It is a real thing. It's a real thing.

And we definitely struggle
quite a bit at our early stage
of the business because the customers,
like they're on a holding pattern,

like, "Hey, we want to
wait until things die down

before we can place a
order" if they have supply.

So we have been trying
our best to have our,
some sort of price guarantee,
Even though we can't control

the tariff piece,
- Right.
- but we can optimize our supply chain,

we can negotiate a price
down with our manufacturer

and absorb some of the
additional costs to try our best
to meet the customer's price expectation.
And so with that, like,
and trying to let customer not to worry
about all the logistic in terms

of like importing and
exporting those things
and we handle that completely
to offload that stress for them.

And then slowly I think, even
though things still going on

and a customer giving
some confidence in them

because we still have
like products going back
and forth during that time
and customer's able to receive products
with confidence and then things
are picking up, I would say, yeah.
- That's good. That's good.

And you preempted one of
my questions, which is,

are you using tariffs
as a negotiation tool?
And it sounds like you are to try

and make sure that you
get locked in pricing
and maybe even preferential pricing.
- That's right. That's right.

We are, because we know a
lot of business here now,
they are not dealing with the tariff

and then they're not
import-export experts.
We want to make sure they're not,
we wanna have a separate of concern
because we are handling the logistic,
we're handling the supply chain.

We want to make sure we put
that responsibility on us
so you don't have to worry about it.
- Makes sense. Makes sense.
So if someone wants to engage with you
or engage with your company

and maybe get a quote
on a production order,
what's the best way to do that?

- I would say we're
doing a lot of marketing
and then you'll probably see our website
from here and there.

Maybe from your channel, they
will see our name pop up,

and they will definitely be
able, we have very clear,
how you work with us, how you contact us,
place order on our website, very detailed,

and then we have a
phone, toll-free number,
you can reach us directly.

And yeah, basically just like
upload your project specs

and we will have our code
team analyze your project,

give you a quote within
a short amount of time
and then we can get it started from there.
- Okay. What's your website?
- Our website is tapren.com.
- tapen.com, okay.
Go over to tapren.com if you're interested

in producing overseas,
but you might be concerned

about some of the logistical
and quality issues,
these guys can really help you out.
Tristan, thank you so much for being here.
- Thank you so much, Zach.
- Thank you. Thank you for having me.
(bright music)

title: Overcoming Global Supply Chain Obstacles in Electronics
